newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro traders scramble to cover Moslem grain demand.
newsitem.headline: Euro traders scramble to cover Moslem grain demand.

text.p: Frantic European traders are scrambling to cover an upsurge in grain offtake from Arab state buyers ahead of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan that starts in mid-January, exporters said on Friday.

Because the European Commission will hold its last tender for 1996 on December 19, anxious operators know they have little time left to secure the licences needed to cover unexpected end of the year business.
Some exporters are even arguing in favour of a special EU refund targeted to north African states, traditional outlets for EU grain.
"The Commission will be closed for two weeks. Those that did not grab licences will be stuck," one exporter said
The Commission has confirmed there will be a two-week gap due to the holidays with the first grain auction for 1997 to be held on January 9.
Excited traders had bid on Thursday to export 1.3 million tonnes of wheat at the weeekly grain aucion.
The Commission ended up awarding 477,700 tonnes of soft wheat. This followed an award of 430,000 tonnes the previous week.
But traders said these tonnages were still not sufficient to cover the strong import demand from Arab states and operators are expected to again massively bid for wheat exports on December 19.
"All Arab states are in the market," one trader said.
Egypt, Turkey, Algeria and Tunisia have already made substantial wheat purchases while Morocco, Yemen, Pakistan and Iraq are also in the market for wheat. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
